SMTO-JOB-0002 — This risky step can't run in the background

GUID: 7a20043d-b8ae-4d18-a93f-d52c4d7257d2
Slug: unsafe-background-unsupported
Domain: JOB · Subsystem: job

What happened

  • SMTO tried to run a risky action, such as a delete or restart, as a background job. SMTO only runs risky actions as normal commands, where they can be checked first, so nothing was run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, ask SMTO to run that step as a normal command instead of in the background. Normal commands go through SMTO's safety check for risky actions, which can ask for your approval; background jobs can't.
  2. If SMTO asks for your approval, check the computer and the command it shows. Select Approve once only if it is what you want; otherwise select Deny / stop task. Your approval applies to that exact action, so checking it first prevents surprises.
  3. If you didn't mean for this risky action to happen, tell SMTO not to do it, or select Stop. Nothing has run yet, so stopping now leaves everything as it was.

What success looks like

  • The step runs as a normal command (after your approval, if SMTO asks for it) and shows its output.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Asking SMTO to repeat the same step in the background will be refused the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The unsafe-action policy denied an unsafe operation requested as a background job (native_job_start) because unsafe actions require captured foreground execution.

What this means

  • The unsafe-action policy guard detects an unsafe operation requested through native_job_start instead of captured foreground execution. Job identity, supervision and dispatch/terminal receipts own effect truth. Diagnostics do not launch, cancel or replay work; missing output or failed control does not prove that the original process stopped.

Why this can happen

  • The unsafe-action policy guard detects an unsafe operation requested through native_job_start instead of captured foreground execution.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the operation's unsafe classification and requested execution mode; ordinary background permission does not satisfy this boundary.

How to fix it

  • ExecutionEngine._preflight_invocation denied the call under execution.unsafe_action_policy because the action is unsafe-classified and native_job_start was set without terminal execution. Re-issue it as captured foreground execution; the Security › Unsafe actions setting (Run blindly, Ask, Disallow) then decides whether it runs, asks for owner approval of the exact action, or is refused.
  • Use the supported foreground approval or job mechanism.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The same intended action uses its supported exact foreground approval and execution path.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Job identity, supervision and dispatch/terminal receipts own effect truth. Diagnostics do not launch, cancel or replay work; missing output or failed control does not prove that the original process stopped.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
